questions.question: How do you gather and document requirements for a new project when stakeholders are not sure what they need?
key_points: Interviews, workshops, observation and document analysis
Focuses on the underlying business problem, not the requested solution
Documents as user stories, use cases or a requirements document
Validates with stakeholders and defines acceptance criteria

questions.question: Two senior stakeholders give you conflicting requirements. How do you handle it?
key_points: Understands each side's goals and constraints
Brings them together with data on impact and cost
Links the decision to business objectives and priorities
Escalates to the sponsor or decision owner when needed
Documents the agreed outcome

questions.question: How do you prioritize a backlog of requirements when there is not enough time or budget to deliver everything?
key_points: Uses a framework such as MoSCoW, value versus effort or RICE
Weighs business value, risk, dependencies and cost
Involves stakeholders in the trade-offs
Revisits priorities as things change

questions.question: Describe how you would analyse and improve an existing business process.
key_points: Maps the current state, for example with BPMN or a flowchart
Identifies bottlenecks, waste and pain points with data
Designs the future state with measurable improvements
Plans the change and measures results after rollout

questions.question: Tell me how you would use data to support a business recommendation. Which tools would you use?
key_points: Starts from the business question
Gathers and cleans data, checks its quality
Uses SQL, Excel or BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau
Presents findings clearly with assumptions and limits
Links the insight to a concrete recommendation

questions.question: What is the role of a business analyst in an agile team, and how does it differ from a waterfall project?
key_points: Works closely with the product owner on the backlog
Writes user stories with acceptance criteria
Refines requirements continuously instead of all upfront
Waterfall relies on detailed requirements signed off early

questions.question: Midway through a project, a stakeholder asks for a significant new feature. What do you do?
key_points: Assesses impact on scope, timeline, cost and risk
Follows the change control process
Presents options and trade-offs to decision makers
Updates requirements and communicates the decision

questions.question: How do you define and measure whether a project delivered its intended business value?
key_points: Agrees KPIs and success criteria at the start
Captures a baseline before the change
Measures after delivery and compares with the baseline
Reports results and lessons learned
